title.narrative: Pacific-European Union Marine Partnership Programme (PEUMP)

description.narrative: The overall objective of this project is to improve the economic, social and environmental benefits for PACP states arising from stronger regional economic integration and the sustainable management of natural resources and the environment. The project purpose is to improve economic, social and environmental benefits from sustainable management of oceanic and coastal natural resources with due regard for the conservation of native biodiversity and climate change adaptation requirements

title.narrative: (O4.5) Number of Pacific maritime boundary datasets supported through the programme is provided for fisheries monitoring, control, surveillance(MCS)

description.narrative: (O4.5) Number of Pacific maritime boundary datasets supported through the programme is provided for fisheries monitoring, control, surveillance(MCS)

comment.narrative: O4.5 By 2018 no provision of data from SPC for fisheries MCS existed before the PEUMP programme started

As per the Service Law Agreement SLA between SPC and FFA the data delivery is sectioned into three phases. Phase 1 and 2 were completed and delivered to the FFA in June and December 2020 respectively. Phase 1 consists of the Exclusive Economic Zone 200 nautical miles layers. These are the individual countries EEZ and the global EEZ. Phase 2 consists of the Terrestrial Sea Zone 12 nautical miles and the Contiguous Sea 24 nautical miles layers. Similarly it consisted of individual countries 12M 24M as well as the global 12M and 24M. Phase 3 consists of the closed areas or marine protected areas MPA and other specific areas that countries have legislated to be protected. Phase 3 has been prepared and will be continuously updated until the end of the programme with regards to the MPAs and specific areas. The results of the work under the phases are used to feature and updated on the Pacific Maritime Boundaries Dashboard httpspacificdata.orgdashboardmaritimeboundaries

comment.narrative: O4.4 By 2023 progress towards the agreement of 4 new maritime boundary treaties

The latest treat signed was between Fiji and Solomon Islands that was signed during the 51st Pacific Islands Forum PIFS summit in Suva on the 11th of July 2022. Other work has been ongoing during Year 5 to progress maritime boundaries treaties for other country boundaries. The following describe some of this progress 21st Maritime Boundaries Working sessionThe 21st Pacific Maritime Boundaries Working Session was convened inperson from 516 December 2022 at the University of Sydney Camperdown Campus. The purpose of the working sessions was to allow national maritime boundaries teams a dedicated opportunity to work on technical and legal tasks organise relevant meetings receive specialised training access experts share success stories and set action plans to progress their work on maritime zones.Deposit clinic in New York in the margins of BBNJ At the 21st Pacific Maritime Boundaries Working Session in Sydney 516 December 2022 the complex nature of entry into force treaty registration and deposit processes was highlighted as an obstacle to the conclusion of some maritime zones in the region. Several Pacific Island countries have signed agreements on their shared boundaries but have yet to ratify these treaties register and deposit them with the UN formally and officially entering them into force. Of the 36 shared boundaries under treaty 8 remain to be entered into force. Completing these deposits is a means to achieveSDG14 Target 3C to implement UNCLOS and aligning regional action with the Pacific Island Leaders Declaration. UNCLOS 101 Training for Kiribati and FijiOn the 19th 23rd June 2023 SPC hosted 3 participants from Kiribati government and 4 participants from the Fiji government for capacity building on basic knowledge of the United Nation Convention of the Law of the Sea UNCLOS.Technical training with Palau supports ocean management through defined maritime zones At the 2022 Our OceanConference His Excellency Surangel Whipps Jr. President of Palau launched an initiative to develop a marine spatial planning process to guide the sustainable management of Palaus exclusive economic zone EEZ. In support of this effort Palau is progressing an ambitious programme to define its maritime boundaries limits and zones including the outer limits of its extended Continental Shelf eCS. From 17 April to 21 April 2023 the maritime boundary team hosted a training for 2 staff both male from the Land and Resource Information System Office PALARIS Palaus national geospatial office. The oneweek professional attachment provided an opportunity to review the countrys maritime boundaries and complete related technical activities including finalizing territorial sea baselines.

Throughout Year 4 international expert Dr Nick Pilcher continued his work to finalise the regional extinction risk assessment for the six turtle species. In October 2021 SPREP published the A Review of the Status of Sea Turtles in the Pacific Ocean 2021 . Being the most comprehensive literature review undertaken for the Pacific region to date it presents a summary of the relevant publications and knowledge about sea turtle reproductive biology movements and connectivity and presents these alongside relevant threats that in combination are pertinent to understanding the status of sea turtle populations in the Pacific Ocean. Dr Pilchers review has not only informed the development of the extinction risk assessment model for sea turtle regional management units in the Pacific but also the development and regional endorsement of the Pacific regional Turtle Action Plan as part of SPREPs Pacific Islands Regional Marine Species Programme PIRMSP 20222026 the KRA 5.4 funded National review of the current state of marine turtle management and conservation in Vanuatu and the development of National Action Plans for Turtles in Vanuatu. Link to Review of the Status of Sea Turtles httpslibrary.sprep.orgcontentreviewstatusseaturtlespacificocean2021 The turtle risk assessment report will be finalised during Year 6 and Year 7.
